item.title: Off-Meta Minute: Amber Amethyst Merida
item.description:
Disney Lorcana|competitive

Off-Meta Minute: Amber Amethyst Merida

Muuuuuum! It's just my bow!

By Scott Mines

|@HowlingMines
|

Published Nov 18, 2026

|

4 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series:

Deck diversity has always been an appealing part of card games for me. As a competitor, I tend to prefer narrower metagames that are easier for me to target, but as a person? Let me turn up to my weekly event and play against every different flavor of nonsense out there. I wanna see what kind of brew gets you out of bed in the morning.

That's a big part of why I started Off-Meta Minute here on TCGplayer. If you cook up something cool, you deserve your flowers. Somehow, I have the platform to give them to you while also encouraging up-and-coming Illumineers to give your madness a shot. It's one of the coolest parts of my job.

Sometimes it's difficult to give the right person flowers, though. Sometimes, a sweet archetype pops up, and I cannot quite place where it originally came from as it lights up the tournament tables like wildfire.

That's what happened with Amber Amethyst Merida.

ELJ_GHartuck's Amber Amethyst Merida - 186th Place at Disney Lorcana Challenge Villain Challenge: Gaston 

I'd also like to mention Liam Dolecki's Top 256 performance with this archetype in DLC London's Main Event 1. The deck clearly has competitive legs; I just like GHartuck's list a little better.

This deck is a side grade to the more popular variants of Amber Amethyst with a few cute tricks baked in. We'll start with the namesake card, Merida - Wisp Conjurer.

 

We don't get Merlin - Rabbit or Genie - Wish Fulfilled anymore, but you can still accelerate into a pair of four-cost Amethyst characters that can draw you cards. You can lean on Mickey Mouse - Best in Town or Hamm - Piggy Bank within your first two turns to curve cleanly into a copy of Merlin - Profoundly Curious (who refunds you for the help) or a difficult-to-contest Merida - Wisp Conjurer that immediately draws a card and threatens to snowball out of control.

 

The best follow-up to Merida is often just a second copy, who can enter play exerted to draw you two cards in tandem with her counterpart. That's not enough to build a deck around though, so you'll need to rely on some other friends to help maximize the number of cards you can score from Merida. How do you do that? Bodyguard.

Rex - Protective Dinosaur is the best cheap bodyguard in this ink combination, regularly trading up for bigger characters and scoring you some lore in the process. Lionheart - Incumbent Mayor is an absolute tank with impossibly difficult stats to push through. Both will gain you incidental lore while banking cards of Merida, leading to an opponent who is frantically trying to bust through the wall to stop the card advantage while falling further and further behind.

But my favorite piece of spice? Remember Me. In those long, grindy games, it's not uncommon for an opponent to think they're running you out of cards before a Merida and a Hamm sing this backbreaking song, allowing you to play like three characters from your discard exerted and draw a card off every single one. You don't want to draw too many of these, so I like having only a single copy — but it's an army in a can all by itself.

 

I alluded to it briefly when talking about Rex and Lionheart, but this deck can close the door shockingly fast once those cards get spinning. Merlin's Shop and Smithy - Magical Market is an annoyingly sticky location that you can ferry your characters to for some extra lore and card draw. Even better, nobody wants to waste their time removing it. Once you enter the late game with a bucket of leftover ink drops, sometimes it'll just be sitting there waiting to win the game. It's a snazzy piece of cardboard.

I also wanted to mention how well the Demona - Imperious Spellcaster package slots into this deck. Of course, the namesake variant is a beast of a card by itself. It'll happily discard one of those cards you've drawn to turn into a turbocharged Madam Mim - Fox, but it can also fill the discard for a timely Remember Me in this shell. Demona - Betrayer of the Clan is also a phenomenal character to accelerate into with Hamm - Piggy Bank against aggressive decks and loves to be juiced up with Rush.

But the high roll? Use Demona - Scourge of the Wyvern Clan to lock down the opposing board before the Imperious Spellcaster sends her rushing into battle. I've had a handful of games where I've been able to play both of these cards with Remember Me and proceeded to blast my opponent's board to bits. It's very sweet.

Closing Thoughts 

I'm very glad that the Hyperia City metagame continues to offer some room to breathe for players who aren't enamored with Amber Emerald or Emerald Steel. Merida - Wisp Conjurer is an absurdly sweet card that didn't really get any time in the sun when it was released back in Attack of the Vine!, so I'm overjoyed to see players cooking up deck lists that allow her to shine. Is Remember Me the sauce? I don't know for sure, but I can't help but hope.

Have further questions? Let me know over at @HowlingMines on X (formerly Twitter) or @howlingmines.com over on Bluesky! Alternatively, give my other work here on TCGplayer a peek if you'd like another slice of everything nice about your favorite game. 

But until next time. I've been HowlingMines, you've been amazing! 

Stay safe out there — and happy gaming!

item.title: The Biggest Price Spikes in Pokémon This Week - 11/18/2026
item.description:
Pokémon|finance

The Biggest Price Spikes in Pokémon This Week - 11/18/2026

You can't keep a good cat down.

By Corbin Hosler

|@Chosler
|

Published Nov 18, 2026

|

4 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series: Movers and Shakers

I know it's trendy to talk these days about how the Pokémon market is slowing down. About how some of the market is correcting, about how many more cards are printed these days, and about how there's just no future in modern Pokémon chase hits.

And then Delta Reign released, and we watched Raikou ex leap up in price.

Delta Reign Defies the Dip

Will this Raikou ex hold the $105 Market Price it has today long-term? Maybe not. But even as more Delta Reign has entered the market over the last week, we've seen the price of the Special Illustration Rare climb in price, and quite drastically. That $105 Market Price tag it carries today is way up from the $90 it was coming out of the gate last week. Clearly, there's still demand for new Pokémon cards, at least high quality Illustration Rare and Special Illustration Rare cards like Raikou.

Elsewhere in Delta Reign, things are progressing more as expected. The headliner SIR Mega Rayquaza ex is actually outpacing the gold version of the same, and both are sliding down slowly in price since release. The gold version (MHR Mega Rayquaza has predictably slid from $225 down to $210 over the last week, while the true chase of the set, Mega Rayquaza, has dipped slightly from $310 down to under $300.

On the other hand, IR Kecleon has been a bit of a surprise winner from the set, moving from $23 at its low to closer to $30+ today. It's easy to see why, given such beautiful artwork on the seldom-seen Pokémon. Similarly, Mega Golisopod ex 135 has actually inched up from $20 to $25 in that same time.

So if you were wondering whether the unlucky set that had to follow 30th Celebration would have its own share of hits, it looks like Delta Reign didn't disappoint in that regard.

Old Promos Spike Unexpectedly

Mewtwo-EX XY125 originally was available in a Super-Premium Collection, back in 2016. Since then, it's been a very slow—but very steady—climb up to its current all-time high Market Price. Once available for as low as $5, Mewtwo-EX had climbed up to $30 by the time 2025 rolled around—and then more than doubled to $75 by the start of 2026. Somehow, it's only gained steam since.

The current run on Mewtwo-EX began around the end of the summer, when the card first began to push up to the $100 threshold, only to keep going. After yet another strong first half of a month, we saw the Market Price on Mewtwo-EX XY125 push all the way up to a new all-time high of nearly $200, with live Near Mint listings stretching even beyond that.

I don't know if it was the Lugia focus from the Classic Collection in 30th Celebration that started the ball rolling on the Reverse Holofoil Lugia from 2016's Fates Collide, but it's gaining speed now. The card started the summer out at just around $5, but has been on an incredible run ever since. It first climbed up to $10 around September, and this week has begun to push even higher as copies slowly dwindle. Like many older (or in this case, mid-era) cards, the movement here is halting, but it is emblematic of where much of the market is putting its focus these days.

New Promos Predictably Drop

Speaking of cards dropping in price, the 2026 McDonald's set of cards is out and the prices are falling fast, with nothing fetching more than $5 (predictably, Pikachu takes 1st place). These limited-release runs can sometimes get pretty pricey, especially years later, so if you're trying to get a little weird with it and catch all the Pokémon you can inside a Happy Meal, you can complete the release quite easily right now.

And while we are on the subject of promos…

A futuristic Pikachu and a gorgeous piece of Espeon art featuring multiple cameos from other Pokémon? That's a slam dunk of a duo, and both of these new releases are available for an ever-more affordable price. 

As they come out of the gate and the market settles, it looks like Pikachu ex has settled around $20-$25, while Espeon ex is coming in closer to $30. With 30th Celebration product still being rolled out and promos still hitting the market, it's difficult to predict exactly where these go from here, but the price for those collecting 30th Celebration is looking quite affordable—especially compared to those $3,000 RBG Mews.

Ascended Heroes and Destined Rivals Continue to Fall

Finally, let's look at the biggest drop of 2026—coming after the climb of 2026—in Ascended Heroes. The set was full of hits and hugely hyped when it was released, and then things began to climb even higher from there. Mega Gengar ex was once pushing $1,400.

Times have changed, as mass reprints of this and other 2026 sets have absolutely cratered prices on the biggest hits in the set. There's nothing to scoff at in a $550 Mega Gengar ex, but that's down $50 in Market Price this week, and obviously worlds away from $1,400. Similarly, Pikachu ex dropped from $560 down to $520. Of course, it's all relative—these are still insanely good hits from a booster pack.

The same goes for SIR Team Rocket's Mewtwo ex from Destined Rivals, the Team Rocket-focused set that is stacked with cool designs. It also had one of several mega chase cards in Team Rocket's Mewtwo ex, but reprints have similarly brought prices down. This week Team Rocket's Mewtwo ex dropped from $310 to $280. 

Until next week, good luck pulling Rayquaza from your Delta Reign!

item.title: How to Build Fang, Dracai of Blades on a Budget
item.description:
Flesh and Blood|Classic Constructed|budget|casual

How to Build Fang, Dracai of Blades on a Budget

Being loyal to the Emperor doesn't need to break the bank.

By Karol Ruszkiewicz

|

Published Nov 23, 2026

|

7 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series:

If you're looking for a new deck this Classic Constructed season, with a strong baseline and a straightforward upgrade path, Fang, Dracai of Blades might just be the best choice for you.

Why? Well, first of all... the deck just won the most recent World Championship! Despite this prestigious accomplishment, Fang is still reasonably low on the Living Legend leaderboard and the core of his kit is incredibly accessible. The deck is clearly powerful, affordable to step into and should remain in the format long enough for you to benefit from the mastery you'll gain. 

The following decklist is tailor-made to give you an affordable entry point into Fang, allowing you to comfortably learn his play patterns, explore different matchups, and gradually upgrade your deck as you go. Best of all, even the baseline is strong enough to hold its own at your local Armory.

I don't want to strip away the deck's identity to hit a budget. The goal here is to preserve the core game plan and find affordable alternatives for the more expensive pieces. You'll still get to experience what makes Fang such a powerful hero without needing to invest in every premium card right away.

Fang, Dracai of Blades is a hero that requires you to tick specific boxes in order to complete his mini quest, which transforms him into an above-rate machine that'll continue sending blazing hot daggers into the nearest spine. You'll need a carefully curated mixture of efficient defensive tools, draconic powerhouses to keep your Fealty around, and a handful of ways to either mark your opponent or generate that Fealty. 

Equipment

Dynastic Diadem and Braveforge Bracers are absolute staples in Fang. They're the go-to options in the majority of matchups, and both are incredibly accessible, setting you back less than a couple of lattes in Paris. Not a bad start for equipment staples!

Grains of Bloodspill and Valiant Dynamo, on the other hand, are a bit harder to acquire. Don't get me wrong, they're incredibly strong, and I absolutely recommend picking them up once you're looking to play more competitively. However, the alternatives are genuinely solid, if not situationally better than the legendaries, as is sometimes the case with Unity equipment compared to Valiant Dynamo.

Grains of Bloodspill can generate those extra Vigor tokens that help smooth out your turns, but Plating of Unity holds its own defensively. Similarly, while Pillar of Unity might not match Valiant Dynamo's defensive value over the course of a longer game, getting that initial two block can sometimes be a net positive. I'd argue that Kabuto of Imperial Authority is the last piece to acquire, as it's the most niche inclusion in terms of the matchups where you'll actually need it. 

If you already own some generic staples like Stonewall Gauntlet, Fyendal's Spring Tunic, or Balance of Justice, they can all slot in nicely against certain matchups too. Fyendal's Spring Tunic can do wonders against slower decks, while Balance of Justice can help you draw that extra card against heroes like Levia, Shadowborn Abomination or Gravy Bones, Shipwrecked Looter.

Draconic Staples

The beauty of Fang's kit is that the majority of his absolute staples are relatively cheap.

Fire and Brimstone, his iconic one-off, is a rare with plenty of copies available to keep its price low. The same goes for Hunt's End and Long Whisker Loyalty. In fact, Fang's most recent addition Fresh from the Forge is already pennies on the dollar too!

Meanwhile, the core of his Draconic attack reaction package consists entirely of commons and rares. Affirm Loyalty, Searing Gaze, and Blistering Blade are must-includes that you're bound to find among your The Hunted bulk. 

This is one of the biggest advantages of building Fang on a budget. You're not compromising on the cards that make his engine function. Most of your savings come from replacing expensive equipment and a handful of premium utility cards, rather than cutting the essential pieces of his game plan.

Marking and Fealty Generation

Fang's quest to reach three Fealty tokens also relies heavily on commons and rares. Pledge Fealty, For the Dracai, and Scar Tissue are instrumental in getting the ball rolling. In this build, I've replaced [Perforate](Perforate (Yellow) with extra copies of yellow Scar Tissue, as it's a great way to double down on generating Fealty by marking your opponent.

For the Emperor also makes an appearance to further increase Fealty generation and help you consistently reach that magical three-token threshold in the early turns of the game. I've also added extra copies of Den of the Spider, giving us yet another way to mark the opposing hero. Consistently marking your opponent and generating Fealty against a marked hero helps fast-track the deck towards its full potential.

I've included six copies across Twist and Turn and Sharpen Senses, providing additional resource cards that enable big combo pushes on the second cycle while still holding their own alongside the deck's red attacks.

The important thing to understand is that Fang doesn't need to rush every point of damage. Sometimes, establishing your Fealty early and setting up a stronger follow-up turn is far more valuable than squeezing out a little extra damage immediately. Learning when to push and when to build towards your next explosive turn is one of the most rewarding parts of mastering the hero.

Flexible Utility

It feels like a bit of a no-brainer switch to substitute Shelter from the Storm for Fate Foreseen. In the majority of cases, it fulfils a similar defensive role, while the opt can prove surprisingly beneficial. Saving a Hunt's End near the top of your deck for the second cycle, anyone?

As you upgrade, I'd recommend focusing on the matchups you're struggling with rather than simply buying the most expensive cards first. A carefully chosen sideboard option can make a much bigger difference at your local Armory than a legendary that only provides a marginal improvement in your most common matchups.

If your priority is to instead flesh out your collection of Warrior cards that you'll get serious value from regardless of which hero you fall in love with, I'd recommend prioritizing Provoke and Lessons Learned as heavy-lifting blues. Alternatively, you can dive into Mastery Pack: Warrior instead. 

Mastery Pack: Warrior

One of my favorite aspects of upgrading this deck is that you can pick up plenty of important cards from Mastery Pack: Warrior, which means you can casually enjoy Crack, Shuffle, Play! or Smash Palace: Chorus of Steel and still make meaningful progress towards your fully powered deck.  

Lessons Learned, Blade Flurry and Glint the Quicksilver are all possible pulls from this Warrior-focused product, alongside premium equipment such as Grains of Bloodspill and Valiant Dynamo.

Best of all, this will set you up to continue your journey with the Warrior class. Many of these cards will find a home in other Warrior decks, so you're not necessarily investing in cards that become irrelevant the moment you decide to try another hero.

Closing Thoughts

Whether you're just starting your exploration of the Warrior class or want to give the World Championship-winning hero a go, this budget Fang, Dracai of Blades build is a fantastic place to start. You get access to the core play patterns, explosive turns, and rewarding decision-making that make Fang such a formidable competitor, without needing to break the bank.

More importantly, the deck gives you room to grow. You can start by learning the fundamentals at your local Armory, gradually pick up the premium equipment and utility cards, and eventually work your way towards the World Championship list. Fang still has plenty of room to climb the Living Legend leaderboard, so there is plenty of opportunity to put those skills to good use. 

Who knows, maybe your budget Fang list will be the one taking down the next big event?

item.title: The Top 10 Most Expensive Chase Cards in Yu-Gi-Oh's Magnificent Maestros
item.description:
Yu-Gi-Oh!|collecting|finance

The Top 10 Most Expensive Chase Cards in Yu-Gi-Oh's Magnificent Maestros

Dragons, but extended and shiny.

By Anthony Tachella

|@tinymech
|

Published Nov 24, 2026

|

7 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series:

Magnificent Maestros has now been on shelves for a few weeks. As a result, the market for singles from the set has started to settle and stabilize. Magnificent Maestros features upgraded versions of cards used by the antagonists from the series. so we won't see any Dark Magician support this time around. Instead, we have support for a certain blue-eyed dragon.

This set has a similar print style to Magnificent Monsters, which came out a few months ago, and contains ultra-exclusive Grand Master Rares. These incredibly hard-to-pull cards are serialized as one of a hundred, so pulling one is a huge achievement in itself.

The Most Expensive Chase Cards in Magnificent Maestros

Today, we're going to be looking at the top 10 chase cards in the set, with the exception of the 18 Grand Master Rares, which completely eclipse all the other cards in terms of sheer value. With that, let's see what the most valuable cards are in Magnificent Maestros. 

#10 Unchained Soul Lord of Yama (Starlight Rare)

From the get-go, the top cards in the set are all Extended Art Starlight Rares. Our number 10 card is the only one on the list that isn't new in MAMS. Unchained Soul Lord of Yama originally came out a few years ago in DUNE, and its first release shot Unchained to the front of the tournament scene.

Now, Unchained has a ton of new support in MAMS, and the best Link Monster in the deck has an awesome new Extended Art and a Starlight variant to boot! The new support has shown that Unchained is once again a deck to consider when going into a tournament, so Yama has been steadily going up in price as more and more people start to switch over to Unchained. Right now, it's sitting around the $170 mark.

#9 Crimson Dragon Quetzalcoatl (Starlight Rare)

Yu-Gi-Oh! 5D's is probably the most popular series aside from the original Duel Monsters series.  As a result, it makes sense that this retrained version of Crimson Dragon is one of our biggest hits in Magnificent Maestros.

I don't think this card is all that playable; it's mainly holding so much value because of its connection to the anime series. Also, ya know, the artwork features all five of the Signer Dragons. Kind of awesome if you ask me. This card has been selling for around $230, but very few listings are still around that price before it starts going up to around $350.  

#8 Starving Venom Fusion Dragon, Four Heavenly Dragons (Starlight Rare)

Starving Venom Fusion Dragon is one of the best Super Polymerization targets in formats where DARK monsters are running rampant. Thankfully, even in a format like this, duelists everywhere are still playing cards like S:P Little Knight, which is one of the many generic DARK monsters that gets summoned from the Extra Deck.

Four Heavenly Dragons is really cool because it helps you fuse away multiple monsters. Super Polymerization does that as well, but going Super Poly into Four Heavenly Dragons gives you another interruption on your opponent's turn. This is incredibly powerful and helps justify the hefty price tag this card is currently carrying. 

#7 Rokket Barrage (Starlight Rare)

Rokket Barrage is another new card in MAMS that brings the Rokket deck back to the forefront of the competition. This card is kind of bonkers. You can Special Summon it from your hand by sending Absorouter Dragon from the deck to the graveyard, which then triggers Absorouter. Right there you're looking at a plus-two in terms of deck thinning. This is before you look at its Quick Effect that summons multiple Rokket monsters from everywhere.

Rokket decks have already started topping Regionals post-MAMS, so it'll be interesting to see how this card fares on the market. Just a few days ago, it would have been in the number eight spot, but a recent buyout puts it just above Four Heavenly Dragons. 

#6 Cyber Dragon, the Luminous Mech Dragon (Starlight Rare)

One of the monsters that changed Yu-Gi-Oh forever, Cyber Dragon is back with a brand new retrain! The Luminous Mech Dragon has the same Special Summoning condition as its original counterpart, but it also has two bonus effects on the field. This card provides a huge boost to Cyber Dragon decks, which are already surprisingly powerful sleeper decks.

Since Cyber Dragon is such a popular monster, and the ace monster for one of the most popular characters from Yu-Gi-Oh! GX, it just makes sense that the Starlight Rare version of this card is pushing close to the $275 mark, it keeps climbing and is getting closer to $300 by the day. 

#5 Red Nova Dragon - Burning Soul (Starlight Rare)

While Zane Truesdale is a popular character, no one compares to the King of Turbo Duels: Jack Atlas!

Red Nova Dragon - Burning Soul is a monster of a card. Its artwork fully encompasses what I feel like every Resonator Duelist is trying to accomplish when they Synchro Summon Jack Atlas's signature monsters. It's also super playable, as it gives the Resonator deck access to a powerful boss monster even after getting hit with something like Nibiru, the Primal Being.

This card is currently around $285, but it has only a few listings before it breaks the $300 mark. Given how gorgeous this card is, I can see it staying at this price point for the foreseeable future. 

#4 Cyber End Dragon, the Final Strike Dragon (Starlight Rare)

Cyber End Dragon is back and stronger than ever. Cyber End Dragon, the Final Strike Dragon lives up to its name as the last monster you'll need to summon in a duel. This is a Cyber End Dragon that searches for Limiter Removal and can attack three times with piercing battle damage after you use Limiter Removal. I'm sorry, but you can't tell me this card isn't cool.

Final Strike Dragon is currently around $300, but I see this card going up over time as more people realize how fun of a card it is for Cyber Dragon decks. That isn't even factoring in how playable it is or the anime fans that'll be collecting this card as well. It just has so much going for it. 

#3 Dark Rebellion Xyz Dragon, Four Heavenly Dragons (Starlight Rare)

Let's revisit Yu-Gi-Oh! ARC-V for a minute with Dark Rebellion Xyz Dragon, Four Heavenly Dragons. This card is an upgraded version of Yuto's ace Xyz Monster and is incredibly powerful in Phantom Knights decks, but also has a huge impact in decks like Toons. Last I checked, Toons was one of the biggest decks in the format post-MAMS.

Dark Rebellion Xyz Dragon, Four Heavenly Dragons is primarily just used to Xyz Summon Evilswarm Ophion from your deck and lock the opponent out of summoning Level 5 or higher monsters. That's perfectly fine if you ask me. Since this card is super playable and has immediately had an impact on the meta, it's the third most valuable card in the set. Currently around $350 for the Starlight Rare variant, you're looking at dropping a pretty penny if you want to put this into your Extra Deck. 

#2 Deep-Eyes White Dragon, the Blue Abyss (Starlight Rare)

Alright, we're at the final two cards. Who would've thought that they would both be Kaiba cards? Me. That's who. Kaiba is the ultimate Yu-Gi-Oh! villain; it doesn't matter who you ask.

Deep-Eyes White Dragon, the Blue Abyss is one of the two Blue-Eyes monsters that have both a Starlight Rare and a Grand Master Rare in this set. This card is really neat in Blue-Eyes decks, since it gives you an easy Level 10 monster to summon to the field. This is going to be super-important in Blue-Eyes Decks moving forward, so expect to see people summoning it left and right.

Right now, Deep-Eyes White Dragon, the Blue Abyss in a Starlight Rare is $750, and it doesn't look like it is going anywhere.

#1 Blue-Eyes White Dragon, the White Phantom Beast (Starlight Rare)

Alright, the most valuable card in Magnificent Maestros without looking at Grand Master Rares is sitting at a grand on its own. Blue-Eyes White Dragon, the White Phantom Beast is an absolutely breathtaking card and one of the biggest hits in the set without a doubt.

This card is a staple in Blue-Eyes decks because its effects are absolutely game-ending. It can be Special Summoned from your hand during the Battle Phase and immediately hits your opponent with a Burst Stream of Destruction to wipe out their board.

If your opponent summons this card, just know that the game is over.

Magnificent Maestros is a really cool set! It's Yu-Gi-Oh's second take on a set that feels like Collector's Booster from MTG, and with significantly better pull rates than Magnificent Monsters, you're more likely to hit it big with awesome Extended Art and Starlight Rare cards!

Just remember, if you pull one of these cards we just talked about, or if you see a hieroglyphic pattern on the border of a card, grab a sleeve fast!

item.title: The Best-Selling Riftbound Cards Right Now (November 2026)
item.description:
Riftbound|finance

The Best-Selling Riftbound Cards Right Now (November 2026)

Nothing defies the best-selling card.

By Scott Mines

|@HowlingMines
|

Published Nov 24, 2026

|

7 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series: Bestselling Cards of the Week

Time for me to admit some personal fault on the internet: this article took me significantly longer to write than usual because I've been constantly vibing out to K/DA's Firestarter. It feels like the song has been on loop in my brain for about a month now, but nobody can yell at me about it because it's technically Riftbound related.

Despite a beloved debut in Radiance, I cannot say the iconic K-pop group are also dominating the headlines in game. Riftbound is currently undergoing a metamorphosis at every level in the wake of a heavy-hitting new banlist, and players are feverishly scrambling to find the new hotness ahead of the American Regional Championship.  

In my eyes, that's the perfect time to dive into the wealth of sales data at TCGplayer and figure out what you're all up to. 

 

Will the former mainstays of the format surge in sales as the banlist takes away their toys? Has a testing team cracked the next big thing? Are we simply panic-buying everything in the fear that they'll be no copies left by the time we've figured it all out? It's probably a mixture of the three, but that's what makes it exciting! There's roughly two months until [Legacy] arrives, and we've got no idea which legends stand to become the kingpins of the new format. How do we make a start? Well, I'm the one with the numbers. Let's take some time and crunch them.

The Best-Selling Riftbound Cards Right Now

These are the best-selling cards in Riftbound during November 2026.  

#10 The Good Stuff

An aptly named card to appear on a list like this one. Who doesn't want a healthy dose of The Good Stuff? This little powerhouse can probably put up a fight for the title of "best card in Radiance" at this point, appearing in over 900 published tournament decklists on Riftdecks since release.

It turns out that a repeatable card advantage engine is a great pickup for everyone from Evelynn, Agony's Embrace to Riven, the Exile. It's even better if you're designed to hold like Vex, Gloomist, can rebuy it with Pack of Wonders or simply empty your hand fast enough to ignore the discard on play. 

The Good Stuff? I think you mean The Great Stuff. I'd take a barrel of anything for 15 cents.  

#9 Scuttle Crab

The little nonsense machine continues his reign of terror. Scuttle Crab's price is up almost 50 percent in the last three months because it's unquestionably a staple of the Calm domain. There are very few green decks that don't want perfect information about which threat to Defy.

A zero might guy might seem innocuous, but it's not difficult to scrap together a point or who with a Scuttle Crab that has already replaced itself before learning about the contents of the opposing hand. In a game like Riftbound, knowledge is power. There are very few ways to get this level of knowledge. I'm putting money on Scuttle Crab being a problem in the future. Until then, it's just very good.

#8 Gust

Gust is our first example of the sales power of omnipresent staples in Riftbound. Despite releasing over a year ago, we're still seeing an average of 65 copies sold every day. Some of that will be players who don't want to move their copies around, but most of it will come from new players onboarding into the game.

Gust has always been great, but it saw a meaningful uptick in play when Riven, the Exile was laser-focused on getting into a battlefield on turn two. In the wake of Dazzling Aurora's ban, I'm expecting the small ball metagame to continue. That should cement Gust as a pillar of the format moving forward too.

Even if you're not playing it, your deck will be built with it in mind. That's the sign of a darn good piece of cardboard.  

#7 Rampage

It's been up-and-up for Rampage for a little while now, especially as players stop having regular access to Vendetta at their local game stores. It's the cleanest way for Body to punch an opposing unit hidden in base directly in the face, and that effect is only becoming more valuable.

Theoretically, decks like Rengar, Pridestalker and Master Yi, Wuju Bladesman are big winners in the post-ban world, but Rampage also made an appearance in this third-place Evelynn deck list from a 400-player event this past weekend. Body is looking like a force to be reckoned with, and Rampage will play a big part in that.  

#6 Star-Crossed

You may not be bouncing Elder Dragon anymore, but that wasn't the only reason we were playing Star-Crossed. It's still one of the better reaction speed interactive pieces if you're messing around with on-play effects like Scuttle Crab, Tideturner or Bedeviling Stranger.

While I do expect the play rate of Star-Crossed to drop slightly now that its primary predator has taken a back seat, I think the card is far too powerful as a toolbox piece to forgo entirely. Expect a single copy in main decks with a sprinkle of additional copies in the sideboard as the meta demands.

#5 Stupefy

If it costs one energy and released in Origins, it's a pretty good bet that it's absurdly powerful. Stacked Deck has already bitten the dust and Stupefy won't be the last card on this month's bestsellers list that manages to tick those boxes.

Almost 2500 copies of Stupefy have been purchased from the TCGplayer marketplace in the last 30 days despite an all-time low play rate for the card. Stupefy is an important tool in Pack Ezreal, which should be on the increase post-bans and likely influenced most of these sales. Of course, it's still equally potent in other Mind legends like Kai'Sa, Daughter of the Void, Nasus, Curator of the Sands and Seraphine, Starry-Eyed Songstress.

#4 Bedeviling Stranger

Bedeviling Stranger is one of the most impressive new cards from Radiance, quickly finding a home in the majority of Chaos decks. Evelynn, Agony's Embrace might be the happiest to make use of the hidden keyword on this one, but it isn't difficult to punk an opponent who overcommitted units to play around Star-Crossed with a timely stranger in any deck.

Radiance was opened in a ridiculous amount, so prices on everything are pretty low right now. You can currently snap up your playset of Bedeviling Stranger for under three bucks, which makes it no surprise that they're flying off the shelves. This won't stay true forever. I think there's a decent chance these are five bucks once Radiance is out of print.  

#3 Punch First

Body is such a big winner from the most recent banlist changes, and nothing is more Body than Punch First.  

Everybody is interested in a one-cost +5 might. You don't have to worry about the runes you just lost if your opponent's best threat just folded like a lawn chair.

Punch First is another phenomenal example of how these must-have multi-legend staples begin to trend upwards as demand increases and supply dries up. It's still sitting at a very affordable 30 cents, but it's up 13 percent this month and 116 percent in the last six. You'll never know when any 10-cent common you opened in Spiritforged may be worth a dollar.  

#2 Trifarian Captain

Frankly, I'm a little shocked to see Trifarian Captain placing so highly in the wake of the bans, but a further investigation reveals that the demand for this card was so high earlier in the month that it's carried it through to a silver medal in the wake of Nocturne, Horrifying and Baited Hook's death.

That's not the end of the story, though. Trifarian Captain is an objectively powerful card. There are not many ways to tutor Last Rites and friends. As more gear and units are printed, the captain will only become a more potent consistency tool in finding the cards that make your deck tick.

Still played in Kennen, Heart of the Tempest? Probably. All I know for sure is that 90 copies still flew out the door on the day the banlist came into effect.

#1 Defy

But nothing dethrones the king.  

Over the last six months, Defy has had a stranglehold on the bestsellers list. The Origins common now commands three dollars per copy (check your bulk!) and continues to sell almost 4,000 copies per month. You can never have enough Defy. It is the litmus test of Riftbound.

You'll find three Defy in most Calm decks, and opposing deck lists are built with that in mind. I can never shake the infamous pre-game communications between Rocklho and Prismaticism about a lack of Defy targets. It has me creasing every time and it's the perfect example of the effect that Defy has on Riftbound.

It's a monster of a card. Simple as that.

item.title: Top 10 Most Expensive Chase Secret Lair Cards In Magic: The GatheringByEmma Merriam-Partlow
item.description:
Magic: The Gathering|collecting|finance

Top 10 Most Expensive Chase Secret Lair Cards In Magic: The Gathering

If it's a mechanically new card, it's probably worth something. 👀

By Emma Merriam-Partlow

|

Published Nov 24, 2026

|

8 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series:

Magic: The Gathering continues to expand into the collector space at a blistering pace, offering timely releases of desirable cards from the growing Secret Lair Drop Series. Since 2019, the Secret Lairs have continued to go from strength to strength, adding a mixture of reprints and mechanically new cards along with some new aesthetics, as seen with the recent Dune, SpongeBob SquarePants, and Sonic the Hedgehog collaborations.

With all of this in mind, it is effortless to overlook the value of some of these Secret Lair cards if you have never seen the card before, but in some cases, you're likely getting more value on the secondary market over time due to these limited releases.

Top 10 Most Expensive Chase Secret Lair Cards In Magic: The Gathering

  • Read More: The Most Valuable Secret Lair Bonus Cards in Magic: The Gathering

As mentioned above, Magic is becoming a growing market for collectors (more so with the release of Magic: The Gathering—FINAL FANTASY last year), where these quirky designs and themes can sometimes command a high price. These factors can vary from player demand to relevant pop culture releases, along with the scarcity of the product. With that, let's run down the most expensive non-bonus cards from the Secret Lair Drop Series, which also features cards from the various Secret Lair Countdown Kits.

#10 Demonic Tutor (Secret Lair Artist Series: Kieran Yanner - Normal and Rainbow Foil)

Demonic Tutor is about as staple as it gets for a Commander card, where there's collector interest in owning the stunning version created by none other than Kieran Yanner. Appearing in the gorgeous Artist Series: Kieran Yanner Drop, this printing of Demonic Tutor is one of the nicest ones going. Since the Secret Lair release, this specific printing is becoming one of the most expensive non-bonus cards from the series altogether. There's a deep interest in wanting to personalize decks these days, and this printing of Demonic Tutor offers this in spades.

There's always a need for cards such as Demonic Tutor in Commander, as it lets you find whatever you need and puts the card into your hand. There's no shame in finding a land card off the Tutor, and it is adaptable no matter the situation you're in. Given the evergreen demand for the card, it isn't a surprise to see this printing of Demonic Tutor climbing in value over the last few months.

#9 Dark Ritual (The Art of Frank Frazetta)

Featured in the incredible The Art of Frank Frazetta Secret Lair is Dark Ritual, which is perhaps the most iconic black card ever printed in Magic. First printed in Alpha, Dark Ritual comes with the elegant piece of text to add three black mana to your mana pool. Since the spell itself costs one black mana, it does serve as a one-shot mana acceleration when playing Legacy Constructed or even Commander. When you often see a Dark Ritual cast, it can help cast a Necropotence, Liliana of the Veil, or even Sheoldred, the Apocalypse without much issue. As for the Secret Lair itself, Frank Frazetta is widely regarded as the Godfather of modern fantasy art, bringing noted characters such as Conan the Barbarian to life.

And given how popular Frank Frazetta is in the fantasy world these days, this Secret Lair became popular with players rather quickly, meaning the value of this printing of Dark Ritual rose in value in little to no time. At present, this Secret Lair printing of Dark Ritual is one of the more expensive variants outside of the Alpha, Beta, Amonkhet Invocations, and Judge Promo printings.

#8 Jin Sakai, Ghost of Tsushima (Secret Lair x Ghost of Tsushima - Normal and Rainbow Foil)

Appearing in the Secret Lair x Ghost of Tsushima is Jin Sakai, Ghost of Tsushima, and it's quickly become an expensive card to own from the Secret Lair Drop Series. For four mana you gain access to a suite of exciting abilities that reward you for attacking with one creature to each player at the table. From giving a creature double strike or unblockable, Jin Sakai has quickly become an incredible option to lead a Voltron Commander strategy by slamming a bunch of Aura and Equipment cards to victory. Even with the Secret Lair being available to purchase in late 2025, it sold out almost instantly, with the namesake card already becoming a desirable card to own from the Secret Lair Drop Series.

The reason for this is that Jin Sakai is a mechanically new card, and it's becoming a bit harder to reprint these as in-Magic versions in upcoming releases, meaning there's a pseudo-Reserved List (of sorts) at play here that can hinder the possibility of these cards seeing a reprint soon. As a result it causes the secondary market to wildly fluctuate.

#7 Sol Ring (Through the Wormhole - Galaxy Foil)

Appearing in the highly popular Through the Wormhole Secret Lair, the Sol Ring from this space-tastic release is providing massive value to collectors. In particular, the galaxy foil printing is becoming pricey due to having a unique aesthetic while offering something exciting for Commander players to collect. For as long as Commander has existed, Sol Ring is a must-have card for Commander as it permits you to have explosive starts coupled with ample colorless mana generation.

As a result of Sol Ring's continued presence in the casual format, fancy copies of the artifact often come at a premium as players continue to personalize their Commander decks. While traditional copies of the card can only set you back a couple of bucks, there's evergreen demand for these special variants as they help to express personalization through playing Commander.

#6 Kaalia of the Vast (Tragic Romance - Normal and Traditional Foil)

Appearing in the sultry Tragic Romance release, it didn't take long for Kaalia of the Vast to become a valuable card from this collection. Kaalia is about as iconic as it gets for a commander these days, and is perhaps one of the few that has stuck around despite the power creep since the turn of the decade. Kaalia makes it so you'll throw an Angel, Demon or Dragon onto the battle as she attacks, which is often a Master of Cruelties to one-shot the attacked opponent.

What made this Secret Lair so popular upon release is the "Romantasy" aesthetic it adopts, which is becoming a popular genre since the release of Baldur's Gate 3 a few years ago. There's clearly a secondary market demand with this desirability in mind, and is certainly one way to get more people invested into Magic.

#4 Chrome Mox (Secret Lair: 30th Anniversary Countdown Kit)

Chrome Mox remains one of the must-have mana artifacts you can play in Commander at the minor cost of exiling a nonartifact, nonland card from your hand. If you achieve this, then Chrome Mox taps for one mana of the exiled card's colors, which is excellent if you want to propel on mana in the early turns and cast any threats ahead of schedule. While the Secret Lair printing of Chrome Mox didn't appear in your typical release, it was part of the Secret Lair: 30th Anniversary Countdown Kit where you received thirty individually wrapped cards with a small chance of opening a foil card. Within the pack of thirty cards, Chrome Mox carried the most value upon the Secret Lair: 30th Anniversary Countdown Kit's release.

What makes this stunning printing of Chrome Mox so desirable is that it incorporates art by long-time Magic artist Dan Frazier, who has created works for some of the most iconic artifacts in the game, such as the Moxen, and even the Signets in a separate Secret Lair release. Cards with exotic printings such as Chrome Mox are climbing in price as there's evergreen demand with Commander players who have excess cash to burn, and it's no different with this unique Secret Lair printing that dropped as part of the 30th Anniversary celebrations back in 2022.  

#5 Jaws, Relentless Predator (Secret Lair x Jaws: Terror of Amity Island - Normal and Rainbow Foil)

Appearing in the popular Secret Lair x Jaws: Terror of Amity Island release is Jaws, Relentless Terror, which is another mechanically new card appearing on the list today. For five mana, Jaws creates Blood tokens equal to the amount of damage it deals to a player. That isn't all, as Jaws can deal one damage to each opponent whenever a noncreature artifact is destroyed or sacrificed, and this includes anything from your opponents as well. In particular, Jaws works well with Treasure tokens (as if Treasure players didn't need another win condition), which is the best way to take the card if you intend to build the towering shark as a commander.

You can also add similar effects such as Reckless Fireweaver, Ingenious Artillerist, and Weftstalker Ardent to push more non-combat damage and potentially make quick work of the table as a result. If you aren't feeling Jaws as a commander, then you can play it within a Ragost, Deft Gastronaut and Ob Nixilis, Captive Kingpin Commander decks that share a similar play style while branching into a secondary color.

#3 The Secret Lair x MSCHF: The Zeta Set Cards

Secret Lair x MSCHF: The Zeta Set is one of the more polarizing releases as of late, but it's one that is seeing some movement on the secondary market. While these cards are currently pricey, Wizards of Coast have confirmed the Secret Lair x MSCHF: The Zeta Set release will have another opportunity to buy on December 9 for 24 hours. This means the current secondary market prices aren't guaranteed to stay that high over the next month. However, Chrome Mox (0219), Birds of Paradise (0313), and Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth (0242) are seeing the most value at the time of publication. It seems the color banding treatment printings are much rarer than the other two treatments, which will certainly retain more value over the coming months.

#2 Mox Opal (Dan Frazier's Mox Box: Las Vegas Festival in a Box 2023)

Featured in Dan Frazier's Mox Box Secret Lair (which was part of the Las Vegas Festival in a Box 2023 release) is Mox Opal, one of the more historically powerful artifacts to ever see print. By utilizing Metalcraft, Mox Opal can tap for any color of mana as long as you control three or more artifacts on the battlefield. The card is that good; it was once banned in Modern Constructed but has since returned to the fold since late 2023, leading to incredible price movement (including this very Secret Lair printing) as players look to snap up copies for competitive play. It's this continued interest that has made this specific printing of Mox Opal among the most expensive non-bonus cards from the Secret Lair Drop Series.

Continued competitive demand aside, Mox Opal still sees plenty of play in Commander (especially in competitive circles) as long as there's a good density of artifacts to ensure you can regularly meet the Metalcraft demands. Much like many of Dan Frazier's other Secret Lair cards, this printing of Mox Opal is popular since it incorporates the classic retro frame, which has become well-loved since its revival in Modern Horizons 2. Combining competitive and Commander demand along with the iconic impact Dan Frazier has had in Magic over several decades, it's no surprise to see this become one of the most expensive non-bonus cards to own from the Secret Lair Drop Series.

#1 The Secret Lair Countdown Kit: An Encyclopedia of Magic (2025) and Marvel's History of Heroes (Halo Foil)

Secret Lair Countdown Kits seem to have a couple of valuable cards post-release, especially ones that can appear in halo foil. While you aren't guaranteed to open a halo foil in your Secret Lair Countdown Kit or Marvel's History of Heroes Countdown Kit, several of them look to be valuable with Urza's Saga, Sol Ring, Tainted Pact, and Fierce Guardianship being the highest at the time of publication. These take on a "Magic Advent Calendar" feel, but offer a nice way to collect desirable reprints of powerful cards.

item.title: The Ultimate Black Friday Gift Guide for Pokémon TCG Fans in 2026
item.description:
Pokémon

The Ultimate Black Friday Gift Guide for Pokémon TCG Fans in 2026

When they say they want Pokémon cards, here's what they mean.

By Peter Day

|

Published Nov 20, 2026

|

6 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series:

The holidays are right around the corner! If you're hoping to surprise and delight a certain Pokémon Trainer in your life, you've come to the right place. We have traveled across the land (searching far and wide) to discover the perfect present for every type of Poké Fan.

Buying brand-new sealed Pokémon card products hasn't been easy in 2026. For the past two years, a boom in Pokémon card collecting has led to shortages of sealed product all over the world. While The Pokémon Company International has been reprinting waves of product to meet the demand, and card prices have come down as a result, many sealed products have remained stubbornly hard to find at MSRP.

It's not all doom and gloom, though! A few underrated gems are still totally affordable, and given how hard it's been to find great deals this year, your Pokémon Trainer will appreciate you putting in the legwork for them all the more.

These are the best holiday gifts for players and collectors of the Pokémon TCG in 2026.

Best Stocking Stuffer: Booster Pack

They like Pokémon cards? Get them a pack of Pokémon cards! Every Pokémon booster pack is basically a present already, with a delightfully rippable wrapper and unknown treasures inside.

The booster pack that Pokémon fans want to open this year the most is 30th Celebration, with Ascended Heroes as a close runner-up. Both of these sets contain huge hits that have dominated social media coverage in 2026.

Ascended Heroes has SIR Mega Gengar ex and "Treekachu," while 30th Celebration has the four-figure RGB Mew cards, plus 30th anniversary reprints of Lugia from Aquapolis and Base Set Charizard. 30th Celebration also boasts the best pull rates of any set in 2026, so the odds are higher that your recipient will pull something incredible.

Unfortunately, booster packs of 30th Celebration and Ascended Heroes are priced to match their hype. Plus, they aren't sold individually at retail (though you can get them on marketplaces like TCGplayer).

If either of those facts is a deal-breaker, we'd recommend Delta Reign instead. Not only is this the newest Pokémon set released so far (and the final set of 2026), but it's got the biggest hit of 2026 outside of 30th Celebration and Ascended Heroes: SIR Mega Rayquaza ex.

You can consider Perfect Order, Chaos Rising, and Pitch Black if you know your loved one is hunting a specific card from those sets. If not, Delta Reign will be the safest choice.

Best Gift Under $30: 30th Celebration Poster Collection

If this were a normal year, we'd be recommending the 30th Celebration Booster Bundle, which retails at an MSRP of $26.94. Unfortunately, in 2026 you aren't likely to find that product for less than $60 unless you get very lucky by visiting a major retailer right as it's restocking.

Instead, at this price point we'd recommend getting the 30th Celebration Poster Collection. This collection comes with three packs, any of which might contain an RGB Mew, plus three guaranteed promo cards of three Legendary Birds, and a poster with art from the set.

30th Celebration products have been elusive all year, and any Pokémon fan would jump at a chance to try their luck with the most tantalizing packs of 2026.

Best Gift for Collectors: 30th Celebration ETB

This year, the most sure-fire gift you can give a Pokémon TCG Collector without spending hundreds of dollars is a 30th Celebration Elite Trainer Box.

Elite Trainer Boxes (ETBs) are often considered the "default" Pokémon TCG product due to their price point and how fun they are to open. Each ETB comes with nine packs, a promo card, and loads of goodies. The boxes themselves are sturdy, and fans love them for card storage and display.

Many Pokémon TCG collectors try to get a Elite Trainer Box at every set release. Because 30th Celebration ETBs were so hard to find in person and expensive to buy online when they first came out, many fans had to put this dream on hold. Receiving it as a gift will feel like all those months spent longing are finally being rewarded.

There are arguably better Pokémon products near this price point. A Delta Reign Booster Box offers far more packs per dollar. The 30th Celebration Ditto Premium Collection comes with an acrylic card display that I personally prefer over any of the goodies in an ETB.

But the sheer quantity of stuff in an ETB, and its stature in the community, make it the most gift-y-feeling option.

Best Gift for New Players: Mega Lucario ex League Battle Deck

In previous years, it was easy to recommend that new Trainers pick up a copy of the most recent Pokémon TCG Battle Academy if they wanted to learn how to play the Pokémon TCG. Unfortunately, there hasn't been a new Battle Academy since 2024, and those boxes are way more expensive than a tutorial product should be.

For now, there are no Pokémon TCG products we can recommend to brand-new players. Instead, we'd recommend that new Trainers who can read on their own learn to play with the official Pokémon TCG Live app. It's 100% free (with no in-app purchases).

Once they know how to play, if your Trainer wants to face off against friends and strangers at a school club or game store, we recommend buying them a battle deck—specifically a League Battle Deck. These "Play Level 3" preconstructed decks come with a complete 60-card deck, and they're extremely powerful right out of the box.

The deck that won the 2023 Pokémon World Championships had 39 cards in common with the Mew VMAX League Battle Deck!

This year, the League Battle Deck we most recommend is built around Mega Lucario ex, a hard-hitting attacker with a few major tournament finishes to its name. Most of the cards inside (including Mega Lucario ex itself) will be legal through 2027.

The non-"League" battle decks like the Umbreon ex and Espeon ex Battle Deck don't offer near as much power, but if one of them features your Trainer's favorite Pokémon, it will still be fun to play. It's just not likely to win a tournament.

Best Gift for the Trainer Who Has Everything

So you're shopping for a certified Poké Maniac. How can you knock their Wooloo fleece socks off them this year?

Every year around November, The Pokémon Company International releases a new Ultra-Premium Collection (UPC) designed to be the must-have gift of the season. This year, that UPC comes in two versions, based on the promos and the theme of the accessories inside.

Inside the Day or Night 30th Celebration Ultra-Premium Collection (UPC), Pokémon collectors will find a whopping 29 booster packs of the most exciting set of 2026. They'll also find two foil promo cards, a small mountain of goodies, and a bonus booster pack exclusive to these products with three cards from the 30th Celebration Classic Collection.

If money is no object and you just want to watch your favorite Trainer's jaw drop lower than it's ever dropped before, look no further. The 30th Celebration UPCs are the most coveted Pokémon TCG product you can buy in 2026.
